courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
courses.description: Introductory course that surveys various fields in linguistics, including first/second language acquisition, phonetics/phonology, morphology/syntax, semantics/pragmatics, language variation, computational linguistics/natural language processing, and writing systems. Credit not allowed for both LING 2100 and LING 2001.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Applications of Linguistics
courses.description: Explores the relation of language (and linguistic theories) to real-world domains including language acquisition, education, gender, advertising, politics, law, and medicine. Taught in English.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Permits students to work in languages not treated in other courses and/or engage in special language research.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Advanced Language Processing
courses.description: This flexible course explores computational-, psycho-, or corpus linguistics (depending on instructor expertise). Students read/present academic articles, process data using Python/R/Qualtrics, and pursue original projects.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Language & Computers
courses.description: A linguistic perspective on language processing topics (search, vector semantics, document classification, digital humanities, translation, dialog). Students read current literature and implement concepts in Python.

courses.subject: LING
courses.title: Japanese Applied Linguistics
courses.description: This course helps to develop analytical skills to better understand human languages, particularly English and Japanese. Taught in English. Credit not allowed for both LING 4780 and JAPN 4780.
courses.prereqText: LING 2001 or LING 2002; LING 2001 or JAPN 2001.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level LING 2001 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level LING 2002 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level JAPN 2001 Minimum Grade of D)
